title.narrative: Livelihood Security in a Changing Environment - Mashonaland East

description.narrative: GOAL 1: A registered network of organic producer associations, with increased productive capacity, status and access to markets. GOAL 2: Public policy influenced towards the formal establishment of Zimbabwe’s organic sector. This innovative project will respond to the challenges presented by decades of dependence on expensive agricultural inputs - resulting in dramatic biodiversity and livelihood loss affecting the smallholder sector - for which there are few avenues for advice and marketing of their, often derided, natural produce. This project will promote a shift in production methods by providing intensive training in OCA and on-farm support to 672 smallholders - encouraging diversification and species adaptation, to increase production and distribution of food and plant-based agricultural inputs to local markets. Raising the status of resource-poor natural producers via organic registration and advocacy is an important strategy which will capitalise on increasing domestic demand for organic produce – currently serviced by South African imports. This hands-on approach requires the training team and consultants to be on the ground to undertake expansive on-farm support, detailed market research/advocacy, PAR and M&E in order to fine-tune and prepare for roll-out to other provinces - creating linkages to CARE's business skills, and savings & lending programmes.
